summary: Frontend-only retest of the landing hero timelapse perf fix — Fix (D) code-split AmbientHeat via React.lazy. Code-split is verified working (separate chunk src_components_AmbientHeat_jsx.chunk.js loaded). hero-fallback with 3 animated blooms paints at ~410ms on cold visit (huge win). Cold time-to-timelapse-stamp improved from 25.5s → 14.0s (~45% faster). Cache-hit time-to-timelapse-stamp improved from 12.6s → 7.6s (~40% faster, ~1.67x). The <5s cache-hit target was missed but the >2x-vs-iter4 improvement direction is real and the user-visible cold experience is dramatically better because the hero is no longer blank while the deck.gl chunk downloads. All regression checks pass except a stale non-blocking issue (3 duplicate /v1/map/timelapse requests on fresh visit).

integration_issues.issue: Target <5s for cache-hit timelapse-stamp appearance; measured 7573ms (vs 12620ms in iter4). Improvement is real (~40%) but target not met. DCL alone on reload was 3810ms on this preview host — the remaining ~3.7s from DCL→stamp is React hydration + lazy-chunk fetch + first frame render. Further reduction would require preloading the AmbientHeat chunk (e.g. <link rel=preload> in index.html for the emitted chunk hash) or eager-mounting on cache-hit.

Fresh visit still fires 3 requests to /v1/map/timelapse (all identical). window.__PULSE_TIMELAPSE_PROMISE__ is still 'object' after full paint — either resolved-promise reference or the resolved data. Not user-visible; wastes tunnel capacity.

On the reload path, AmbientHeat inner wrapper transform read as matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0) at ~7.6s after nav — i.e. no 11% translateX applied. In iter4 (non-lazy) it correctly read matrix(1,0,0,1,211.2,0). Possible cause: because the settled state is scoped to LandingPage and AmbientHeat now mounts after the lazy chunk resolves (which is after the 700ms setSettled timer already fired), the transition never fires and inline style is applied — yet the computed transform shows 0. Worth a quick look — the copy-drift-left is still applied on the LandingPage side so this only affects the heat drift-right cosmetic. On cold visit this may be less noticeable because the chunk loads before/close to the timer.

action_items: OPTIONAL: To hit the <5s cache-hit target, consider adding a <link rel=preload as=script> for the AmbientHeat chunk in index.html so the chunk downloads in parallel with the main bundle, or use `import(/* webpackPrefetch: true */ ...)` on the lazy() import to emit a prefetch link.

OPTIONAL: Investigate why AmbientHeat inner wrapper transform reads matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0) on cache-hit reload despite settled being true when it mounts. Cosmetic (heat drift-right vs stationary), no user-blocking impact.
OPTIONAL (carried from iter4): dedupe fresh-visit /v1/map/timelapse request count (3→1).
critical_code_review_comments: Code-split boundary is well-chosen: AmbientHeat.jsx cleanly encapsulates all deck.gl imports (DeckGL, HeatmapLayer, OrthographicView), so the main-bundle no longer needs to parse @deck.gl/aggregation-layers. HeroFallback lives in LandingPage.jsx and paints from the main chunk — good architecture.

Consider adding `/* webpackPrefetch: true */` magic comment on lazy(() => import('../components/AmbientHeat')) — this emits <link rel=prefetch> so the browser fetches the chunk during idle time after main paint. Would likely close the 2.5s gap to hit <5s cache-hit target.
The Suspense fallback={null} + sibling HeroFallback pattern is correct and defensive — if the chunk fails to load, blooms stay visible. Good.

success_rate.frontend: 95% (all functional checks pass; cold-visit hero now paints in ~400ms; cache-hit target <5s narrowly missed at 7.6s)

rca of the issue: Cache-hit paint time dominated by two factors on this preview: (1) DCL alone is ~3.8s (CRA dev bundle over tunnel), (2) React.lazy chunk for AmbientHeat is fetched only after main bundle parses and Suspense boundary mounts, adding ~3.7s more. React Query initialData from readTimelapseCache IS consumed immediately once AmbientHeat mounts (stamp shows frame N/43 from cache without a network wait), so the cache mechanism itself works — the delay is purely bundle/hydration cost, not data availability.
